Guizhou Tourism Development Commission.desc: A tourism department of the Guizhou provincial government in south-west China, at full provincial-department rank (正厅级建制). Its stated responsibilities include carrying out national tourism law and policy, drawing up and implementing the province's tourism development plans, running tourism resource surveys and statistics, approving travel agencies, supervising tourism market order and safety, and promoting Guizhou as a destination; its 2018 budget covered nine internal departments plus the Guizhou Provincial Tourism School, the provincial tourism quality supervision office and the provincial tourism information centre.

No claim is made that the Commission was merged into 贵州省文化和旅游厅 in the 2018 reform: the only thing pointing that way is the folder name 'gzswhhlyt' in the hosting path, which is page metadata and not a statement by anyone. Left as a lead in the report.

Tanzania Electric Supply Company Limited.desc: State-owned electricity company in Tanzania and the country's public electricity utility, carrying out generation, transmission, distribution, supply, cross-border trade and system operation. It accounted for 91% of installed generating capacity and 99.50% of electricity customers as of June 2024.

Not re-fetched this round.

Kurasini Oil Storage Company Limited, fo.note: Absent source, and the renaming inside the key could not be dated either way. Searched for both names together and separately with Dar es Salaam oil-terminal terms; what returned was the Kurasini oil jetty and the state TIPER terminal, which are different things, plus trade-press terminal news naming neither company. Tanzania's company registry (BRELA) search was not reachable through the tools available here, and no gazette notice, filing or news page naming either name was opened. The Tshs 1,638,111,700 payment and the identity link between the two names rest on the January 2014 resettlement-plan amendment the card already cites.

Rail Assets Holding Company (RAHCO).desc: A Tanzanian state-owned company incorporated under the Railways Act 2002, whose whole issued share capital was held by the Treasury Registrar. Its objects were to take over the rail transport functions and certain property of the Tanzania Railways Corporation and to develop, promote and manage the rail infrastructure assets on behalf of the government, holding the Railway Infrastructure Fund on irrevocable trust and able to delegate operations to other operators, usually by concession. The Act under which it existed was repealed on 28 February 2018 by the Railways Act 2017, which established the Tanzania Railways Corporation.

Rail Assets Holding Company (RAHCO).why: Written from the establishing statute, not from the web. Two limits recorded rather than papered over: the 2002 Act does not say RAHCO owns railway land (it refers to rail infrastructure assets held by the company and limits transfers to a lease), so the card's 'held Tanzania's railway land' is not repeated here; and the 2017 Act's repeal and transfer sections (113, 114, 116) sit past the point where the fetched text cut off, so the repeal date comes from TanzLII's own repeal note on the 2002 Act, with the 2017 Act cited for the Corporation's establishment and its commencement dates (most sections 28 February 2018, transfer of assets and liabilities 30 June 2018, by Government Notice 65 of 2018).

Volta River Authority.desc: Ghana's state electricity generator, established in 1961 by an Act of Parliament and solely owned by the Government of Ghana. It combines hydro, thermal and solar plants, selling to the Electricity Company of Ghana (61% of market consumption) and directly to mines and industry, and for export to Communaute Electrique du Benin (for Togo and Benin) and SONABEL in Burkina Faso; its subsidiary NEDCo distributes electricity in northern Ghana.

Volta River Authority.why: Same body as 'Volta River Authority (VRA)' already written and checked in rounds/r26f_companies_8b_checked.json; carried over verbatim for consistency with that entry. Not re-fetched this round.

Ghana Grid Company Limited (GRIDCo).desc: Ghana's electricity transmission utility and system operator, incorporated in December 2006 and operational from August 2008, with the Government of Ghana as sole shareholder represented by the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Energy. It is licensed by the Energy Commission to operate the National Interconnected Transmission System exclusively, dispatching and transmitting electricity from wholesale suppliers to bulk customers and distribution utilities in Ghana and West Africa, and its mandate has been extended to commercial telecommunications over its transmission assets. It transmitted 23,551 GWh in 2023 against a peak demand of 3,618 MW, and its registered name was changed to 'Ghana Grid Company LTD.' in August 2023.

sources.title: GRIDCo 2023 Annual Report
sources.publisher: Ghana Grid Company Limited

Ghana Grid Company Limited (GRIDCo).why: From the company's own annual report. Two figures deliberately left out: the report's network size (about 6,639 circuit km, 66 substations) carries no date in the report, and its revenue appears twice with different values (GH¢2,265.457m in the income statement and CEO report against GHS 2,247.156m in the corporate highlights), which is a source inconsistency and is reported rather than resolved. The 1963 Companies Act registration and the 2019 Act under which it is now governed are in the report; only the name change is dated to 2023.

Societe Nationale d'electricite du Burki.desc: Burkina Faso's state electricity company, set up by the state as a societe d'Etat with a board of directors and governed by Law 25/99/AN on state companies. Its share capital of 46 billion FCFA, in 4,600,000 shares, is assigned entirely to the Burkinabe state. Its stated object is production and transmission of electricity, and it holds exclusively the distribution, import and export of electricity throughout the national territory.

sources.title: Décret n° 2004-517/PRES/PM/MCE portant adoption des statuts de la Société nationale d'électricité du Burkina (SONABEL), articles 1, 2, 3 and 6 of the annexed statutes

Societe Nationale d'electricite du Burki.why: From the establishing instrument rather than the utility's own pages. The capital figure is the statutory capital in the 2004 statutes and is dated as such, not given as a current balance-sheet number; no customer, generation or revenue figure is claimed because none was in a source opened. Note the decree's own name for the company is 'Société nationale d'électricité du Burkina', without 'Faso', while the key and common usage include it.

Eiffage Energie Systemes.desc: One of the business lines of the French Eiffage group, working as a turnkey contractor on electricity infrastructure; its 'Transport & Distribution' unit carried out the Bolgatanga-Ouagadougou interconnection, a 225 kV overhead line of nearly 200 km with the Zagtouli and Patte d'Oie substations in Ouagadougou, built between October 2016 and January 2018 and inaugurated on 5 October 2018.

Eiffage Energie Systemes.why: Deliberately thin, to avoid describing the parent and presenting it as the subsidiary. The group's own page lists Eiffage Energie Systemes among its business lines and names a unit beneath it, which is what the government-body rule asks for, but no page opened gives this entity's legal form, revenue or headcount, so none is given: the Eiffage group's 25.3 billion euro 2025 revenue belongs to the group and is kept on the separate 'Eiffage' entry. Searches for an entity page returned only job boards and market-data aggregators, which COMP.md excludes. The project detail is included only because it is what identifies the entity on this page.

Communaute Electrique du Benin (CEB).desc: An international public body (organisme international a caractere public) of Benin and Togo, created under the Benin-Togo electricity code annexed to an international agreement between the two governments. Its capital is held by the two states in equal shares, and under article L5 of the code it holds exclusively, across both territories, the activities of transmission, importation and single buyer, acting as sole buyer for both states' needs and sole supplier to the distribution networks.

sources.title: Décret n° 2005-014 du 21 janvier 2005 portant ratification de l'Accord international portant code bénino-togolais de l'électricité, with the code annexed (article L5)

Communaute Electrique du Benin (CEB).why: From the ratified instrument. The exclusivity is given as the code states it, in the present tense of the instrument; a 2015 Financial Afrik headline says CEB lost its purchasing exclusivity, which was not opened and is not claimed here — it is recorded in the report as a lead. No size figure is given because none appeared in the instrument.

SAE, bought by GAMMON in 2015 and GAMMON.note: Blank for the Poyry reason: the names match too many entities rather than none, and nothing opened ties any of them to this Benin contract. No document giving the legal form of the contractor in the key was reached, so nothing is written in either direction. The 2015 and 2017 restructurings stay on the card from the completion report, undated by any second source.

Societe Beninoise d'Energie Electrique (.desc: Benin's state electricity company. Its statutes were set by Beninese decree 89-123 of 30 March 1989, when it was named the Societe Beninoise d'Electricite et d'Eau and also ran urban water supply and wastewater; decree 2003-203 of 12 June 2003 created the Societe Nationale des Eaux du Benin, transferred that water responsibility to it and amended article 4 of SBEE's statutes accordingly, leaving electricity. Since January 2024 its management has been delegated to the Eranove group under a public-private partnership covering electricity distribution and commercial operations across the country, with an initial term of 26 months.

Agence Beninoise d'Electrification Rural.desc: A Beninese public establishment with a non-profit purpose, holding legal personality and organisational and financial autonomy, placed under the supervision of the ministry responsible for energy. Its mission is to support the state's rural electrification and energy-efficiency policy: preparing national and regional programmes and pilot projects, overseeing energy audits and certifying equipment efficiency, setting technical standards for rural electrification, preparing tender files for rural electricity concessions, and mobilising and managing the rural electrification fund. A 2018 decree on off-grid electrification makes it the conceding authority for off-grid public electricity service and the body that authorises off-grid systems of 500 kVA or less.

Naming note: the heading of the 2004 decree reads 'Agence Béninoise d'Electricité Rurale et de Maîtrise d'Energie' while the body and the key read 'Electrification'; both forms are in the same instrument and neither is treated as the one correct name.

Multan Electric Power Company (MEPCO).desc: A Pakistani state-owned electricity distribution and supply company, incorporated on 14 May 1998 as a public limited company under the government's unbundling and corporatisation of the power sector, taking over the assets and liabilities of the former Multan Area Electricity Board; it is now registered under the Companies Act 2017 and licensed under the electricity regulator's legislation, with almost all shares held by the Ministry of Energy (Power Division). It supplies 15 districts of southern Punjab — Multan, Muzaffargarh, Kot Addu, Layyah, D.G. Khan, Taunsa, Rajanpur, Lodhran, Bahawalpur, R.Y. Khan, Khanewal, Sahiwal, Pakpattan, Vehari and Bahawalnagar — across about 105,505 square kilometres, and in financial year 2024-25 reported 8,816,400 consumers, 16,569 million kWh sold and 13,705 employees.

'Almost all shares' rather than a percentage, because the report's two shareholding entries total 1,092,362,604 shares against a stated total share count of 1,082,464,604 — an internal inconsistency, reported rather than resolved. The regulator's report supplies the general fact that every distribution company except K-Electric is government-owned; revenue (Rs 524,062 million in 2024-25) is left out as the figure that moves most and is not needed for the sector claim.

Islamabad Electric Supply Company Limite.desc: A Pakistani state-owned electricity supply and distribution company, incorporated on 25 April 1998 (registration L09499 of 1997-98) and categorised as a public-interest public limited company under the Third Schedule of the Companies Act 2017, owned by the Government of Pakistan with the Ministry of Energy (Power Division) as its administrative ministry. Its own legal-status page describes its core function as supplying, distributing and selling electricity, and its area as running from Attock to Jhelum and from the River Indus to the River Neelum in Kashmir. Against a target of 7.80 per cent, its transmission and distribution losses were 8.06 per cent in financial year 2022-23.

The loss percentage is used rather than the energy volumes in the same table because that table does not label its units. The card's point that IESCO's area extends into Azad Kashmir is consistent with the company's own river-boundary wording, which is as far as the page goes.

Lahore Electric Supply Company (LESCO).desc: A Pakistani electricity distribution company incorporated in 1998 under the Companies Ordinance 1984, with 100 per cent of its shares owned by the Government of Pakistan and a board of directors; NEPRA issued its distribution licence (No. 03/DL/2002) on 1 April 2002. It serves five Punjab districts — Lahore, Sheikhupura, Kasur, Okara and Nankana — with a population of about 25 million, and reported about 6.04 million consumers at the end of December 2022, having billed 25,070 GWh to customers in 2021-22.

sources.title: Application filed by LESCO for grant of Power Supply Licence

Lahore Electric Supply Company (LESCO).why: One source, but it is the company's own filing to its regulator. The incorporation date is given as the year only, because that filing prints three different dates for it: 18 February 1998 in the executive summary, 14 May 1998 in the company baseline, and 13 February 1998 on the scanned certificate of incorporation, with the certificate to commence business on 9 March 1998. Both figures carry the year the filing gives them.

Hyderabad Electric Supply Company (HESCO.desc: Two Pakistani state-owned electricity companies. HESCO was incorporated under the Companies Ordinance 1984 on 23 April 1998, with its registered office in the WAPDA complex at Hussainabad, Hyderabad, to take over the assets, functions and responsibilities of WAPDA's former Hyderabad Area Electricity Board; it distributes and supplies electricity in Hyderabad, Tando Allah Yar, Tando Mohammad Khan, Badin, Sujawal, Thatta, Jamshoro, Matiari, Shaheed Benazirabad, Sanghar, Mirpur Khas, Umerkot and Tharparkar, and its December 2023 licence makes it supplier of last resort in that territory for 20 years from 27 April 2023. Against a target of 18.63 per cent, its transmission and distribution losses were 27.49 per cent in financial year 2022-23. NTDC is a wholly public-sector company holding transmission licence TL/01/2002, granted on 31 December 2002 for 30 years, with exclusive rights as grid company for the whole country except the K-Electric service area at voltages of 220 kV and above; a modification approved in March 2023 removes system-operator functions from that licence, to be licensed separately, with legal separation required within two years.

HESCO's ownership is claimed only through the regulator's general statement that all distribution companies except K-Electric are government-owned: its own licence states no shareholding. NTDC's incorporation date and law are not given because the licence document does not state them, and 'wholly public sector entity' is the regulator's own phrase. The territory list is the one printed in the determination; the licence's Schedule-I defines the area by maps and codes rather than a district list.

Kampala City Council, later the Kampala.desc: The city government of Kampala, Uganda. The Kampala Capital City Act, assented to on 28 December 2010, published in the Uganda Gazette on 14 January 2011 and commenced on 1 March 2011, provides in section 5(1) for an authority known as the Kampala Capital City Authority, makes it the governing body of the capital city administering the city on behalf of central government (section 5(3)), and provides in section 4(2) that any entity which existed as a local government in the delineated area ceases to be a local government on commencement. Its chief executive is an executive director appointed by the President on the advice of the Public Service Commission (section 17), and the minister responsible for the capital city has general powers to give policy directives and may veto decisions that appear illegal (section 79).

sources.title: Kampala Capital City Act (Chapter 195), sections 4, 5, 17 and 79, version of 14 January 2011
sources.publisher: ULII (Uganda Legal Information Institute)

Kampala City Council, later the Kampala.why: Written from the statute, which is the route for this material. The renaming in the key is dated rather than overwritten, and deliberately given as the Act gives it: the Act creates the Authority and strips local-government status from whatever existed in the area, without naming the Kampala City Council — so the card's 'the elected City Council was replaced' is consistent with the Act but is not a phrase the Act uses. The version read is the 14 January 2011 text, which ULII marks as not the latest; a Kampala Capital City (Amendment) Act 2022 exists on the Ugandan parliament's site and was not opened, so nothing here is claimed as the current law.

President's Office - Regional Administra.desc: The Tanzanian government office that runs regional administration and local government: its own site says it oversees the 26 regions of Tanzania, coordinating between central government and the local authorities, and supports councils, districts, municipalities and cities, including overseeing health, education, road, water and other public-facility projects delivered through them.

President's Office - Regional Administra.why: Thin on purpose. The office's own page gives its functions and the figure of 26 regions but cites no establishing instrument and no founding date, so none is claimed; the brief's rule against describing the territory instead of the body is met by sticking to what the office does and the tier of bodies beneath it. Route note: www.tamisemi.go.tz/administration returned an empty shell page titled 'GWF CORE'; the same path on the host tamisemisitelive.tamisemi.go.tz served the content.

COPRI.note: Absent source, and the name is too short to resolve safely. Searched together with the E60 Agara to Zemo Osiauri section and with the Georgian roads department; the department's own contract-award list (georoad.ge) does not name COPRI at all, and nothing else opened names a company of this name as a contractor anywhere. With no document giving a legal form, a country or a sector for this name, a description would be guesswork about which of several possible firms is meant.

Blacksea Group.desc: A road-construction company registered in Tbilisi, Georgia. The Roads Department of Georgia's own contract-award record prints the name as 'Company Black Sea Group LLC' with a Tbilisi address, and lists it as an evaluated bidder on four lots of road works on the Samtredia-Chokhatauri-Ozurgeti-Kobuleti and Chokhatauri-Bakhmaro roads, with read-out prices from 9.5 to 21.6 million lari, each of which went to China Road and Bridge Corporation.

sources.publisher: Roads Department of Georgia (georoad.ge)

Blacksea Group.why: One of my two weakest entries, and the reason is the name test. The key is 'Blacksea Group'; the only official document reached prints 'Company Black Sea Group LLC', which is probably but not demonstrably the same firm, so the entry says what the state roads authority's record prints and nothing more. The completion report's 'one of the largest construction firms in Georgia' is not repeated, because nothing outside that report supports it, and the lots listed here are a different project from the case. The sector claim rests on the company appearing as a bidder for road works in the roads authority's own tender record, not on the words inside its name. Gulf News's 'Black Sea Group: your partner in infrastructure projects' was not used: it sits in that paper's sponsored GN Focus section, which COMP.md excludes.

Searched in French for MIK with the Maluku special economic zone, Kinshasa, Africom and the zone's operator; results were Congolese press and the ACP state agency on the zone's tenants (Refriango, South Korean firms) and the ministry's count of seven zones, none naming MIK, plus the Bank's own project documents, which are what the card already rests on. The joint venture between the Congolese state and Africom stays on the card from the completion report, unconfirmed elsewhere.

Strategos.note: Absent source. The name appears in the completion report's annex 8 as the private developer of a public-private partnership signed on 28 January 2020, and nothing opened in the Maluku zone searches names a company called Strategos, its country or its legal form. The name also matches many unrelated firms, so this is the Poyry situation in miniature: too many candidates and no document tying one of them to the zone.

Artelia.desc: An engineering and project-management group whose capital is held entirely by its managers and employees. It provides consulting, master planning and feasibility studies, design and engineering, construction and project management, asset and facility management and turnkey solutions, in mobility, water, energy, buildings and industry. Turnover was 1.15 billion euros in 2024, about half of it outside France, with 9,800 employees at 31 December 2024 and operations in more than 40 countries.

sources.title: Artelia Essentials 2024
sources.publisher: Artelia Group

Artelia.why: The group's own publication, with both figures dated to 2024 as it dates them. No nationality or headquarters is claimed: the publication does not state where the group is incorporated or headquartered, and 'about half generated outside France' is a revenue split, not a statement that the group is French. The employee shareholding is given as the publication puts it (100 per cent held by managers and employees, with a target of at least 50 per cent employee shareholding), with no breakdown claimed.

British Engineering Services.desc: A British electrical engineering contractor: the legal entity behind the site is BES (Europe) Ltd, registered in England and Wales with company number 3934096, branded as BES Group with 'British Engineering Services' in its header, with a registered office and UK headquarters at 27 High Street, Horley, Surrey, and overseas work through branches, offices and affiliates. It says it designs and installs power plants, transmission lines and substations, with work in Africa and South America, and lists Sierra Leone among the countries where it works, naming the National Power Authority and the Ministry of Energy there.

sources.title: Where we work — Africa
sources.publisher: BES (Europe) Ltd / BES Group (beseurope.com)

British Engineering Services.why: The nationality and the registration number are claimed because the company's own site states them, not from the name. The identity link to the case rests on this firm doing electrical installation work in Sierra Leone with the National Power Authority and the energy ministry, which the page states; the page does not mention Freetown or this project, and the card's own quotation is from the Bank's completion report, so nothing is claimed about what it did on the line. No revenue or headcount figure was on the page, so none is given.

Electricity Distribution and Supply Auth.desc: Sierra Leone's electricity distribution body: it owns and operates the country's main grid and its isolated grids, and is responsible for the distribution network, for connections and for electricity sales to customers.

sources.title: Enhancing Sierra Leone Energy Access Project (P171059), Stakeholder Engagement Plan, sections 1.3 and 4.2
sources.publisher: World Bank / Government of Sierra Leone

Electricity Distribution and Supply Auth.why: My other weakest entry, and the reason is the restatement test: 'responsible for the distribution network and electricity sales' comes close to restating the name, and what carries the entry is the separate statement that the body owns and operates the main and the isolated grids. The statute route failed and the failure is a robots rule, not a blocked host: the National Electricity Act 2011 (Act 16 of 2011, assented and commenced 15 November 2011 according to SierraLII's metadata page) sits on parliament.gov.sl, which refused the fetch as robots_disallowed, and old.sierralii.org/node/5304 carries only the Act's metadata and a download link, not its text. So nothing is claimed about EDSA's establishment, its legal status, its board or the National Power Authority's dissolution, and the card's 'successor to the National Power Authority' is not repeated here. The only source is a development-bank project document, which is secondary about the institutions it names.

Centre for Accountability and Rule of La.desc: A Sierra Leonean civil society organisation based in Freetown, which says it is committed to promoting human rights through accountability. With two Sierra Leonean health workers who contracted and survived Ebola, it filed a case in the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice on 1 December 2017 claiming that government mismanagement of Ebola relief funds violated the rights to life and health.

sources.title: Centre for Accountability and the Rule of Law et al v. Sierra Leone
sources.publisher: Open Society Justice Initiative

Centre for Accountability and Rule of La.why: Thin, and from a co-counsel's case page rather than the organisation's own. Route note worth carrying: carl-sl.org, the organisation's domain, now serves a page advertising an online gambling site and no longer carries any content about the organisation, so the usual own-site route is gone. Nothing is claimed about founding date, staff, offices or funding, because nothing opened states them. Note also the naming difference: this page and the ECOWAS case title use 'Centre for Accountability and the Rule of Law', with 'the', while the key omits it.

Marino Enterprise.note: Absent source. Searched for the name with Timor-Leste, Dili and road construction; the only official host reached, the government's eProcurement portal (eprocurement.gov.tl), served a published award document that names a different vendor (Reza Construction, Unip. Lda) and does not mention Marino Enterprise at all, and the remaining results were aggregator directories and business-profile sites that COMP.md excludes. The firm is named only inside the project's updated resettlement plan, which records a complaint about its work and is not a description of the company.

South African National Parks.desc: South Africa's national parks agency. It was first established under the National Parks Act 57 of 1976, now repealed, and operates under the National Environmental Management: Protected Areas Act 57 of 2003; it is a public entity under the Public Finance Management Act, listed as a Schedule 3 Part A public entity, and submits its five-year strategic plan for approval to the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment as its executive authority. Its mandate is to conserve, protect, control and manage national parks and other defined protected areas and their biological diversity, and it says it manages 21 national parks covering over four million hectares of land and almost 370,000 hectares at sea, about 70 per cent of state-owned terrestrial protected areas, with five parks part of transfrontier conservation areas shared with Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Mozambique and Lesotho.

sources.title: Legislative and constitutional mandate
sources.publisher: South African National Parks (SANParks)

sources.title: Overview — SANParks profile
sources.publisher: South African National Parks (SANParks)

South African National Parks.why: Both pages are the agency's own. The park and area figures carry no date on the page, so they are given as what the agency says it manages rather than as figures for a stated year — flagged here because the brief rules out figures with no year, and these are counts of current holdings rather than a reported annual figure. The department named is the one the page names, including the page's own DEFF abbreviation for a department whose current name it spells out as Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment; no minister is named because the page names none. Employee numbers are not given: the overview page does not state them.
